key_insight: A reverse-to-forward curriculum with paired advantage signals helps LLM agents learn long-horizon tasks by first mastering states closer to reliable success.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a training strategy for tool-using agents facing sparse terminal rewards and difficult exploration.
method: Define a capability region: states from which the current policy can reliably complete the task.
Use paired advantages to separately reward reaching more solvable states and completing tasks from them.
Expand competence backward along successful reference trajectories, then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration.
evidence_signal: On ALFWorld and WebShop, the method outperforms competitive agentic RL baselines, reaching 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% success, respectively, with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct.
watch_item: The curriculum uses successful reference trajectories; their acquisition cost and the method's robustness to reference quality are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
